host: Linux amd64, Intel Core Ultra 9 285K, Go 1.27.3, CGO disabled, GOMAXPROCS=4, taskset CPUs 0-3
protocol: Three fresh processes; five synthetic FP32 generation cases; 24 alternating-order pairs per case; complete baseline and candidate runtimes are package-renamed into one executable. Every completion JSON is compared outside timing. Common interface boxing remains inside timing.

observations.bulk_directory: Fresh 32-page allocation: 70 objects before, 65 after, measured with AllocsPerRun(10). Data buffers and individual page objects remain separately allocated. Only the page-pointer directory grows in one operation.
observations.workspace: A fresh single direct session leaves both validation maps nil. Multiple sessions still create/reuse the duplicate-cache map; pooled sessions still create/reuse the reservation aggregate map.
observations.latency: Across-process medians of paired ratios are approximately -1.7% to +0.7% across the five conditions. Individual process medians span approximately -2.5% to +2.0%. This does not establish a uniform speedup.

validation: Regression tests fail on baseline for unnecessary maps and repeated directory growth.
Single/batch/single transitions, rejected duplicate batch without position/page/capacity changes, and subsequent retry pass.
Page boundaries, non-growing calls, existing page identities and contents are preserved.
Normal complete Go suite, targeted race tests, vet, build, CLI smoke, five isolated probe builds and Python tests pass.
retention: No cross-request workspace or KV pool added.
No speculative KV payload pages allocated for possible future tokens.
Existing KV and activation admission checks remain in place.
Page-directory capacity follows standard Go slice growth and may differ; page payload count/size and activation-array capacities are unchanged by these edits.
scope: Small bookkeeping allocation reduction, not a real-model quality, peak RSS, GC-frequency or serving-throughput claim. Attention callback reuse is deliberately excluded and reviewed separately.
